clue.text: Young lady of Spain in a store, wandering about

indicators.note: something wandering about moves aimlessly, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl drifts around inside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish form of address for an unmarried young woman, so it names a young Spanish lady.

clue.text: A fanatic attracts me with good spice

indicators.note: the fanatic draws the next pieces to itself, so they follow on directly

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a fitness nut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A zealot draws the speaker in with some good seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a kitchen spice.

clue.text: Oven-cooked to order: then there must be an R in the month

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or altered, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction mixed with the old rule that you eat oysters only in months containing an R.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to the saying that oysters should be eaten only when there is an R in the month. MBE is a British order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: November is a calendar month, the eleventh of the year.

clue.text: Spanish dish makes a learner jump up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate
to leap is to jump

explanation.surface: A Spanish dish so startling that a novice leaps up.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Valencian rice dish cooked in a wide pan with saffron, seafood or meat.

clue.text: Increase in pets being turned out of bed

indicators.note: being turned over means the letters are shifted around into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: More animals being turfed off the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up a pace or effort is to raise or intensify it.

clue.text: Plaything to observe now and then

parts.note: to see is to observe, in the present tense
then points to the past tense of observe, which is saw

explanation.surface: A toy you only glance at from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' looks like 'occasionally', but it splits the verb into present and past tense, which also describes the toy's up-and-down motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank pivoted in the middle for children to ride up and down.

clue.text: "Dance cancelled", as the umpire might say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: there is to be ..., no dance
second meaning: the cricket umpire's call for an illegal delivery

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, called by the umpire and penalised with a run to the batting side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reads both as a notice that a formal dance is off and as the cricket call for a foul delivery.

clue.text: Leaned over and made up a story about a good man

indicators.note: the fib goes around the good man, so the saint sits inside

parts.note: to lie is to make up a story
ST, short for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: Someone tilted and spun a yarn about a virtuous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists heels over to one side, so it has tilted or leant.

clue.text: Anaemic ghost is cleaner and thinner

parts.note: an anaemic person looks pale or white
a spirit is a ghost

explanation.surface: A pale phantom is cleaner and slimmer than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner and thinner' looks like comparatives describing the ghost; they are nouns for what the solvent does.
explanation.definitionFit: White spirit is a petroleum solvent used to clean brushes and to thin paint.

clue.text: Better religious education given to class

parts.note: RE is the school subject abbreviation
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: School scripture lessons improved by being given to a whole class.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to improve or amend it, making it better.

clue.text: Unthinking man wants editor to take smaller part

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
less means a smaller amount or share

explanation.surface: A careless man wants his editor to accept a reduced role.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means paying no attention, acting without thought or care.

clue.text: Periodical, one for astrologers

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single magazine aimed at stargazers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi, the wise men of the Nativity, were Persian priests and star-readers who followed a star.

clue.text: To get much hotter, shove off!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to burst into flame
second meaning: an angry dismissal, get lost

explanation.walkthrough: The literal sense of turning to fire sits beside the idiom used to tell someone to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both literally as becoming fire and as a rude idiom telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Where Sherlock Holmes used his loaf?

definitions.meaning: the detective lived at 221B on a famous London street
loaf is rhyming slang for head (loaf of bread), so using it means thinking; a baker uses loaves too

explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British slang for think, from rhyming slang loaf of bread for head; bakers literally use loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes lodged at 221B in this London street, where he did his deducing, and the name nods to bread-making.

clue.text: One comic which could be profitable

indicators.note: the letters could be something else once reordered, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian who might turn a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic enterprise is one that pays its way, yielding enough return to be worthwhile.

clue.text: I window-shop, they say, for strips of hair

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the phrase is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: to window-shop is to browse, so I browse

explanation.surface: A shopper describing looking without buying, then oddly mentioning lines of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched lines of hair above each eye are its brows, a pair of narrow hairy strips.

clue.text: Played cricket with solemn person in the hay

indicators.note: the solemn person is placed inside the hay, which surrounds it

parts.note: hit the hay means go to bed, so hay stands for bed
an owl is a solemn-looking, wise-seeming person

explanation.surface: A cricket match played alongside a sombre figure lying in a haystack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball, so bowled describes taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl is to deliver the ball to the batsman in cricket, one way of playing the game.

clue.text: Half the rent is needed by a friend indeed

parts.note: the first half of the word rent, its first two letters
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A tenant needs a mate to cover half the rent, truly.
explanation.definitionFit: Really and indeed are both intensifying adverbs meaning truly or in fact.

clue.text: Unusually cool reason for drawing trains

indicators.note: letters arranged in an unusual way are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: An oddly calm explanation for sketching railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but here it means pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive is the engine that hauls a railway train along.

clue.text: Out-of-date headgear is tediously familiar

parts.note: old means out of date
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: An unfashionable cap is wearisomely well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale and over-familiar, no longer novel.

clue.text: Removing a fish's head is making a mistake

indicators.note: taking something away signals that a letter is dropped
head points to the front of the word, the letter that is taken off

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Gutting and beheading a fish is the wrong thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong, so erring means committing an error.

clue.text: Flat affair doesn't finish

indicators.note: the word does not reach its end, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an event is an affair or occasion

explanation.surface: A dull occasion that never quite ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Even describes a level surface, synonymous with smooth and flat.

clue.text: Flowers for a dog getting ill, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone imagines bringing blooms for a sick dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall garden plants with spikes of showy blooms, named for their sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Bank is broken by a river once in a blue moon

indicators.note: the first word is split open by what follows, which goes inside

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riverbank breached by its river only at long intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a riverside, but it is the verb meaning depend on.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in a blue moon is an idiom for very seldom, infrequently.

clue.text: Pass on, concealing sensitivity and love

indicators.note: the outer word hides the inner one inside it

parts.note: to pass on is to die
an ear for music is a sensitivity to it

explanation.surface: Dying while hiding one's feelings and affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie and love are both affectionate British terms of address, like darling.

clue.text: Nevertheless, many wayfarers must have swallowed it

indicators.note: the words swallow the answer, holding it inside across their join

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the two words, from the end of many into the start of wayfarers

explanation.surface: Travellers have, despite everything, gulped something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway and nevertheless are both sentence adverbs meaning in spite of that.
